new.statement: The Muon recipe is untuned for this net. It uses airbench94_muon CIFAR-10 defaults (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, batch 2000, tuned for 64/256/256) and carries SGD-era components (Lookahead, triangular warmup, 64x BN-bias LR). Retuning it toward the Hiverge/airbench94_muon settings (batch ~1536, linear decay with no warmup, no Lookahead, per-step weight renormalization, LR floor) raises sample efficiency enough to cut epochs.

Prediction (exchange rate under Muon): the Muon incumbent at 8.5 and 9.5 epochs gives an accuracy slope of 0.6-1.2 pp/epoch. The marginal pp/s from this slope becomes the reference for re-scoring E009 and E010.

Prediction: on the Muon incumbent at a fixed epoch count, removing Lookahead and replacing the triangular schedule with linear decay from the start (no warmup) changes 3-seed mean accuracy by >=+0.2 pp, and per-step time does not rise.
Prediction: batch 1536 with Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 (Hiverge), at the same epoch count, beats batch 2000 / lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 by >=0.2 pp in 3-seed mean, with <=3% more time.

Prediction (attribution): Nesterov SGD at batch 2000 with 9.0 epochs (lr rescaled airbench-style) lands >=0.4 pp below E007's Muon run (0.7544). If so, E007's gain comes from the optimizer, not from the batch-size change.
Prediction: ending the LR decay at 5% of the peak instead of 0 (as Fable does) raises 3-seed mean accuracy by >=0.15 pp at a fixed epoch count on the Muon incumbent.

Per-step cost concentrates in the high-resolution group-1 layers (32x32 and 16x16). It is limited by memory bandwidth (training-mode BN, activation and pooling traffic at batch 1000-2000) rather than by FLOPs. So cheapening group 1 (fewer convs, earlier pooling, fewer BN/activation passes) cuts time more cheaply than cutting epochs, and widening low-resolution layers is nearly free.

new.statement: Prediction: a torch.profiler breakdown of one incumbent step shows >=40% of GPU time in non-convolution kernels (BN, activation, pooling, elementwise), and most of it in the 32x32 and 16x16 stages.

Prediction: under Muon, cutting group 1 to 2 convs (as in E009) and training at 9.5 epochs gives 3-seed mean >=0.755 at <=8.5 s, which beats the E007 incumbent on time while keeping or improving its margin.

Prediction: the E009 vs E010 ranking (depth cut 0.41 pp/s vs width cut 0.82 pp/s) is within noise. Group 1 at 2 convs and width 112, with epochs added to reach >=0.755, is within 2% of the time of the depth-only cut at matched accuracy.

Python and kernel-launch overhead from the multi-group optimizer step (Muon Newton-Schulz per parameter, Lookahead, separate SGD groups) costs a measurable share of step time that compile flags do not reach. Capturing the train and optimizer steps in a CUDA graph, with foreach-fused updates and Newton-Schulz batched across parameters, removes it.

new.statement: Prediction: batching Newton-Schulz across conv weights into one call and capturing the full step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD) as a CUDA graph warmed up in build cuts train time by >=3%. 3-seed mean accuracy stays within 0.1 pp, since the change is numerically equivalent.

Prediction: running the full optimizer step (including Muon/Newton-Schulz and optimizer-state allocation) on synthetic data in build, then resetting state in prepare, removes the first trial's ~0.15 s train-time excess. Trial 1's train time comes within 0.05 s of trials 2-3.

The score is limited by the safety margin, which per-seed variance sets: E007's per-seed range is 0.6 pp, and the 3-seed mean is only 0.14 pp above the bar. Lowering per-seed variance, or measuring perturbation noise accurately, lets epochs be cut while the 40-seed mean stays >=75%.

Noise model: the perturbation noise that matters is how sensitive the 3-seed mean is to internal randomness (data order and augmentation) with the trial seeds held fixed. Its spread, not the run-to-run determinism seen in E003, sets the inconclusive band for deltas.

Prediction: re-running the Muon incumbent 3 times with only an internal augmentation/data-order salt changed gives a 3-seed-mean spread (max minus min) of 0.15-0.4 pp. Deltas below about 0.2 pp are then inconclusive.

Averaging weights late in training (an EMA over the last ~1 epoch, with BN statistics re-estimated or the EMA applied to BN buffers) lowers per-seed accuracy variance and slightly raises the mean in this under-trained regime.
Prediction: adding a weight EMA (decay tuned so it covers about the last epoch) to the Muon incumbent lowers per-seed accuracy std by >=30% and does not lower the 3-seed mean, with <=2% added time.
